chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: How 'After Hours' was made
summary: He recorded Parrish's piano choruses and played drums himself.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: We've talked about "Tuxedo Junction". What about things like "After Hours" and "Tippin' In"?
You know, I didn't tell you how "After Hours" started.

Delores Brown, I had a recording that RCA wanted me to do called "Fine and Mellow". Delores Brown was the vocalist. Now, the arrangement that we had before the vocals came in, Avery would play 4 or 5 choruses.

Now, we was doing this during a dance and everything. Piano solos. So, when we go down to Victor to record the tune, the tune was too long. We had to take all those choruses out. I took them all out except one before the vocal came in. So, we finished "Fine And Mellow".

Now, they want to know what I'm gonna do for my 6th number. I said, 'Give me a half hour.' I pulled that every now and then.

So, I took Avery, Lee, the bass player, Stanfield, Big Jack, the drummer, and McLemore, the guitar at that time. I said 'Avery, you know all those choruses I took out of "Fine and Mellow"?' He said yes. I said, 'Play them all for me right now.'

So, he started playing them and we

started to line them up. After we got them lined up, then we got backed up, brought the band back together, and then we had added an out chorus, you know. And, I had him do, keep tinkling on his piano while we were playing something very simple, something very catchy.

After we got that together, then I told Big Jack. I said Big Jack, I'm not playing in this tune. You, you direct. Let me play drums. I sat down and played drums. I said when I point to you, you bring your hand down for us to start. I was looking at the red light.
So, that's how we made "After Hours". We played it. And, there was no name to it.

Then, I wanted to find out the name to it. Then, I asked for suggestions. Everybody started giving me a name and I put them in a hat. I looked them all over until I got the one that said "After Hours". Then I said this is it. This sounds more like it. One of the controlmen made that suggestion.
I said who was, who put "After Hours"? Then they, from the engineer, he threw
up his hand. And so, that's how we happened to get "After Hours".
He was going right by the feeling.
Now, that's how we happened to get that number. And, I was playing drums.
On the original record. I had to do the wire brushes, soft, you know?
That's it. I didn't have to play nothing. I didn't have to play my instrument. I said Big Jack, I said you direct. You know, we just had a little fun, and we got it together.
